189. **[NEXT after 156, with 187 (attended 2026-10-16, Mark: "how do I now start to use this on other projects? do we have an ailang world skill that needs to be globally available so I can ask the agents in there?")] w-world-onboarding** · clause-5 (MET; adoption) · **USING WORLD ON ANOTHER PROJECT IS A SIX-STEP OPERATOR PROCEDURE, AND NO AGENT CAN BE ASKED TO DO IT.** Measured 2026-10-16 (trial episodes tps-a/b/c, w185, wdocs): per project the operator hand-writes an exec profile (`~/.ailang-world-exec/profiles/<project>.json`), prepares and warms its environment (venvs), mints a session at a TTY (`session new`, with the daemon STOPPED because it holds the store writer lock), restarts `worldd` with `--exec-profile`/`--exec-episode-project`, launches the agent with only World MCP tools and the bearer token (`scripts/trial/trial.py`), then grades, records the outcome and opens the PR. No `ailang-world` skill or plugin exists (only `use-ailang`, for the language). **THE ITEM:** (1) a global `ailang-world` plugin (sunholo marketplace, like ailang-parse): a skill teaching agents to work through World (`workspace-exec` not shell, `why`/`provenance` to explain changes, outcome records) and an MCP entry that reads the session token from a file, never the repo; (2) `ailang-worldd episode start <repo> --task …`: branch + worktree + mint (still a human-typed y; minting must work while a daemon serves, e.g. via the daemon, without weakening the human-typed rule) + daemon start/reuse + the launch line; (3) `ailang-worldd profile init`: propose an exec profile from pyproject/go.mod/Makefile for the operator to approve. The skill can never mint (authority rule). Needs a design; row 188 may later turn the mint into a desktop approval. · filed 2026-10-16 (attended). **Scope note (attended 2026-10-19):** the skill also covers the OPERATOR side — watching an episode while it runs (`provenance --episode`, `why`, and row 198's `episode report` once it lands) — not only agents working through World.
